record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Put the heuristic connection between quantum chaos and random-matrix spectra on a mathematically rigorous footing.

evidence.quote: A main challenge is to put the heuristic connection between quantum chaos and the spectra of random matrices on a mathematically rigorous footing.

artifact.category_tag: quantum chaos and random matrix theory
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold whose geodesic flow is chaotic (for instance, uniformly hyperbolic, such as a negatively curved surface, or more generally a classically ergodic and mixing system). Consider the Laplace–Beltrami operator $-\Delta_g$ on $M$ with eigenvalues $0 = \lambda_0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots$, and, after unfolding the spectrum so that the mean level spacing is $1$, let $\{s_i\}$ denote the rescaled consecutive level spacings near energy $E$.

The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit heuristic asserts that, in the semiclassical limit $E \to \infty$, the local statistical properties of the unfolded spectrum (e.g. the nearest-neighbor spacing distribution $P(s)$, the number variance, and the $n$-point correlation functions) coincide with those of the eigenvalues of a large random matrix drawn from the appropriate Gaussian ensemble dictated by the symmetry class of the system: the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) for time-reversal-invariant systems with integer spin, the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE) when time-reversal symmetry is broken, and the Gaussian Symplectic Ensemble (GSE) for time-reversal-invariant half-integer-spin systems.

Problem. Provide a mathematically rigorous proof (or disproof) of this correspondence: namely, for at least one nontrivial class of chaotic Hamiltonian quantum systems (such as the Laplace–Beltrami operator on a generic compact negatively curved manifold, or a generic chaotic billiard), establish that the local eigenvalue statistics of the unfolded spectrum converge in the semiclassical limit to those of the corresponding Gaussian random-matrix ensemble.
artifact.status_search_result: The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture, which is the standard formulation of the heuristic correspondence between quantum chaos and random-matrix spectral statistics, remains a major open problem in mathematical physics. While substantial progress has been made for arithmetic and special model systems (e.g., quantized cat maps, certain Hecke eigenvalue statistics, work by Rudnick, Sarnak, Kurlberg, and on band matrices by Erdős–Yau and collaborators), no rigorous proof exists for a generic chaotic quantum system.

status_evidence.title: Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The BGS conjecture, asserting that spectra of chaotic quantum systems follow random matrix statistics, remains unproven for generic chaotic systems.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture connecting quantum chaos and random-matrix spectral statistics is widely regarded as open.
